text:
Mikael Backlund is 37 and in his 18th season with Calgary, the only NHL team he has ever played for, and the start has been rough on the scoresheet: two goals and five points in 16 games, with no power-play points. He's shooting 4.9%.

That last number is the one we'd bet on changing. He's generated 4.1 expected goals and scored two, so the looks are still there, and the Flames have scored almost four fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as one of the league's best setup men last season, 97th percentile in primary shot assists, and still getting to the front of the net.

The harder question is whether he's still a top-six center. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level overall in 2025-26, held up by defense: opponents created noticeably less with him out there. Calgary is getting 47.8% of the five-on-five expected goals in his minutes, so the defensive edge isn't showing yet. Our range has him around 19 goals and 38 points, which would still be a useful season for the captain.
headline: Mikael Backlund is getting chances, not results
